name: ヴィーガンカフェ 楽夢菜 (Vegan Cafe Ramuna (Rakumuna))

gf_detail: Not gluten-free and not celiac-safe. name: さくらパン工房 (Sakura Pan Kobo)
neighborhood: 四条大路 (Shijo-oji), near Amagatsuji Station, west of central N
gf_detail: A gluten-free rice-flour bread (米粉パン) is offered for customers concerned about gluten. However, this is a small wheat bakery whose core lineup is made from 100% domestic (Hokkaido) wheat, and no information about a separate gluten-free workspace, equipment, or cross-contamination controls is published. name: お台所＆サロン かたつむり (Odaidokoro & Salon Katatsumuri)
cuisine: Gallery café in a renovated prewar townhouse
gf_detail: No gluten-free program. The kitchen serves a single daily-changing home-style set meal, and documented dishes include spring rolls and okara (soy pulp) cake; miso and seasonings typically contain wheat, so the food is not celiac-safe. There is one cook preparing everything by hand, so a celiac diner would need to call ahead (0742-25-5366) and discuss specifics; nothing is dedicated or certified.

name: ピーワイハラールキッチン (PY Halal Kitchen)
gf_detail: Not a gluten-free destination. Core menu is wheat-heavy: naan, roti, and noodle/udon dishes all contain wheat, and curries are not prepared as celiac-safe. No dedicated gluten-free practices documented. Rice-based dishes such as biryani may suit a wheat-avoider, but cross-contamination cannot be assumed and no allergen handling is documented; ask directly.
